_comment: THE RUBRIC IS THIS KIT. It is the INPUT (the shape the brief must take), the GOLD (there is
no other — two correct summaries of one document share almost no words, so there is no string
to match), and the COST DRIVER (a person reads against it, priced in reviewer-minutes).
Weights total 100 and are shown on the empty panel deliberately: a reader learns what the
brief is graded ON before anything has run. A rubric that only appeared after a run would let
the shape be whatever the model happened to produce.
The scale is 0-5 per section, not pass/fail. A binary scale throws away the thing a person is
there for. Approved 2026-08-04 at Stop A.

anchors.0: absent, or so wrong it would mislead someone who did not open the source
anchors.1: present but mostly unusable — vague, or contradicted by the document
anchors.2: partly right, with an error or an omission a reader would notice
anchors.3: usable. Nothing wrong, nothing that adds to reading the document's own opening
anchors.4: good. Accurate and specific, missing something a careful reader would have kept
anchors.5: what you would want to receive instead of the document

sections.name: What this document is about
sections.asks: Would a reader who never opens the source know the subject and the scope?
sections.why: The cheapest section to get roughly right and the most damaging to get wrong.

sections.name: Key findings
sections.asks: Are the findings the document's own, and are the significant ones present?
sections.why: The heaviest, because this is what a brief is FOR. Omission is the failure mode, and an omission renders as a shorter section rather than as an error.

sections.name: Numbers that matter
sections.asks: Is every figure carried here in the source, unaltered, with its unit and period?
sections.why: The one section where a hallucination is unambiguous and cheap to catch — a grader can check a number against the document in seconds.

sections.name: What is recommended or required
sections.asks: Are these actions the document calls for, rather than actions the model thinks are sensible?
sections.why: Separates summarising from advising, which is the single most common drift in this task.

sections.name: What the document does not settle
sections.asks: Does it name the limits, open questions and caveats the source itself states?
sections.why: A brief that never says 'unknown' is the tell that it was written from the highlights rather than the document.

sections.name: Who it is for
sections.asks: Is the audience and the decision it supports stated in one line?
sections.why: Light, but it is what makes a brief a brief rather than an abstract.
